mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of two consecutive quarterly GDPC1 declines.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of four consecutive months of below-average INDPRO.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above their respective 12-month averages signals a stagflation risk, which increases uncertainty and discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated increase in both personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth) and retail sales (implied by HOUST) above their 12-month averages for two consecutive months signals robust household demand, which boosts corporate revenues and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both above 12-month averages for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and HOUST are above their 12-month averages for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals persistent labor market weakness, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 12-month moving average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of six consecutive months of below-average PAYEMS.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in real personal savings (implied by RSAFS growth outpacing income growth from PAYEMS) over four consecutive quarters signals a shift from consumption to saving, which reduces near-term demand and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth exceeds PAYEMS growth for four consecutive quarters
regime_hint: household deleveraging or precautionary savings regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS growth exceeds PAYEMS growth for four consecutive quarters.
